summary: Verified 'N days in status' chip feature on customer profile order timeline — backend tagging + frontend rendering. 6/6 pytest cases pass; UI flow (paid → shipped → delivered) verified end-to-end via Playwright.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2107 lines — still over the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting endpoint modules by domain (orders, customers, pricing, notifications).
In get_customer, days_in_status is silently skipped on ValueError/TypeError when parsing the timestamp — logging a warning would help catch data-quality issues.

days_in_status semantics: delta.days floors sub-24h to 0 but the chip label still shows hours in that case (nice), but boundary at exactly 3.0 days shows amber correctly. hours_in_status uses floor of total seconds; consistent.
seed_data_creation: Test creates ephemeral customers (name prefix ZUITEST_/TEST_dis_) and orders against an existing product. Customers are deleted at end of run; a few orders remain but are attributed to now-deleted customer emails.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests in /app/backend/tests/test_days_in_status.py cover: (1) fresh paid order has is_current_status + days_in_status=0 on order_created event; (2) after status change to shipped, chip moves to the shipped event and order_created is untagged; (3) terminal statuses (delivered/cancelled/refunded) strip is_current_status from ALL events for that order; (4) multiple open orders each independently tagged. UI verified via Playwright by creating customer/order via API then navigating through Customers sidebar → search → row click; testid `timeline-age-<order_id>` renders slate tone at 0 days, disappears when delivered. Amber/red tones not tested end-to-end (would require backdating created_at in DB — no such helper exists) but color logic is straightforward if/else in TimelineEvent.
